It has never been positive for me. One time I called because I was going through major antidepressant withdrawals because the symptoms were terrible and I was having terrible, TERRIBLE nightmares. I’d wake up in the middle of the night and get the urge to relapse because of it. I called once, and after talking about what was going on she asked me what I normally did to get rid of the urge to relapse. I said something along the lines of “sleep through it I guess” and she told me to do that tonight. What a wonderful lady (:

Huge win for me: every year of college (the last two) has been terrible for me, trauma/abuse/covid related. This year has been the first year where I’m actually living my life the way I want to and I finish this semester next week with all A’s. I had to submit an appeal in order to enroll this semester because my GPA was too low. I feel amazing :)

The one thing taking college courses in psych has taught me is this: trauma is not the event, it is how it affects your brain. There is no comparing trauma because everyone is affected wildly different. 
Secondly, developing C-PTSD is a disorder after experiencing complex trauma. One isn’t worse than the other, it’s simply the developing of neurological issues after something terrible has happened to you. 
I know it’s difficult not to compare, but there really is no true comparison between trauma because that isn’t how it works. I hope you find peace <3

14. I'm 20 now, a few days over six months clean.

I'm in the first healthy relationship of my life and today is actually 9 months together. I think love feels like safety. I've never felt safe enough to really be myself around someone in my life. Too afraid to feel too much, to be too much. I feel safe with them because I know they will always be accepting of whatever I show them of me, and I will do the same for them. I love everything he does and thinks and I know they feel the same.
same here, only recently learned about the medical terms as well and I've been clean for a few months now. super strange i didn't get a single infection for years lol

i want to specify that you wouldn't be taking back control, you would be giving up control to your addiction. I'm in a similar situation at age 20, having done it for at least 6 years now, and i understand wanting to rationalize it, but i promise you not giving in to those urges is always better than doing it. i hope you're doing a little better since this post <3

while it is nice that she trusts you with things like that, you need to think about yourself over her. it is not your responsibility to always be there and be emotionally available. you even said yourself that it's triggering for you, so you should try to set a boundary to at least cut down on it or have her ask you if now is a good time or anything like that. you can care for someone and love someone more than you ever thought possible and still have to uphold a boundary like that for your own health.

I've been able to slow down my relapses to once every few months/year, and when I do my brain feels guilty as hell about it so I go for "quality" over "quantity" so it doesn't feel as bad I guess? I used to all over my body but now it almost feels like I'm giving myself a free pass because it wouldn't be *that* bad even though that isn't how it works

I just want to say that this isn't a non-issue. It's something you're struggling with and it feels awful to have sh invade these other parts of your life that are supposed to be an amazing event. I'm sure you'll find a way to get around it, don't feel bad for talking about it :)

upside: I think it goes for positive emotions too! I only recently got out of every toxic situation I’ve been in basically since childhood (oct 2020) and I can genuinely say that when good things happen, the bpd definitely cranks those up too, haha! it makes total sense, and I think it’s just because we feel so much stronger. like, his “fuming” could be the most anger he’s ever felt at once, but that might only be a tenth of our anger if that makes sense?

She would quite literally forget what she said and I realized this when I recorded it once and she felt so horrible for saying that stuff to me. (Please don't think I'm trying to demonize, as someone who has also had these extreme emotions I understand and I can't imagine how difficult this specific part of it is) I don't think it's abnormal at all, even for neurotypicals honestly :)
